text:
maya: Helm is stuck in a wait loop creating gpu-pool in eu-west-1a. terraform apply returned partial success. canary ramp is at 20%

deploy-bot: rollout started for release/gpu-pool v3 -> weight 10%

ops-bot: alert: ASG scaling failed for nodepool-gpu-eu-west-1a (InstanceLaunchFailure)

sanjay: seeing new instances in ASG but they never attach to SG, kubelet joins then immediately NotReady taint.

liam: terraform state shows desired_capacity=4 current_capacity=0 for aws_autoscaling_group.nodepool-gpu-eu-west-1a

maya: i think there is a race: TF created ASG but instances fail during launch due to wrong iam/profile name; helm is waiting on DaemonSet pods on nodes that never become Ready.

casey: can we pause the canary? /rollout pause? @jen are you oncall?

jen: paused canary weight. we have autorevert after 5m if health checks fail — currently holding.

sanjay: found config mismatch: iam_instance_profile name is "nodepool-gpu-profile-v1" in TF state but module expects "nodepool-gpu-profile" -> instance launch fails on attach.

maya: quick path: update TF var to correct profile, plan shows ASG replacement. but argocd/helm will notice missing k8s resources and keep trying to reconcile helm chart -> might flip-flop with TF changes.

liam: running: terraform apply -target=module.nodepool.aws_autoscaling_group.nodepool-gpu -auto-approve\n
sanjay: terraform plan snippet:
```
-/+ aws_autoscaling_group.nodepool-gpu (new resource required)
  name: "nodepool-gpu-eu-west-1a"
  desired_capacity: "4" -> (known after apply)
  tags: {...}
```

maya: to avoid helm flipflop i'm going to set argocd sync to suspended for gpu-pool while we fix infra. will re-enable and then resume canary manually.

ops-bot: argocd: application gpu-pool: sync paused by maya (reason: terraform reconciliation)

deploy-bot: canary weight set to 0% -> traffic reverted to baseline

casey: after apply, instances launched and joined cluster, nodes labeled gpu=true. kubelet logs show nvidia driver init successful. pods are scheduling.

maya: unpaused argocd, ran helm upgrade with --wait --timeout 10m. bumping canary to 10% and monitoring for 10m before further shift.

liam: note for postmortem: avoid interleaving infra-as-code that brings k8s capacity with helm charts that 'wait' on that capacity. add explicit pipeline gate: terraform apply -> wait for node readiness probe + label -> then helm deploy.

maya: filing a short incident doc with recommended gating and a change to the helm chart to be tolerant of missing nodes (non-fatal wait) for infra-creation flows.

jen: thanks all — nice coordination. :thumbsup:
